root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward darkness and reduced clarity, with branches involving evening or night, impaired or feigned sight, and movement or judgment in conditions of limited visibility.
root_idea.development: The lexical development extends from the darkness and lack of perceptual clarity of night into the evening time, approaching a fire for guidance, turning away or pretending not to see, and acting amid perplexity or uncertainty.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form عَشَا.
Displayed as the temporal noun عَشِيّ.
Displayed as the distinct temporal noun عَشِيَّة.
Displayed as the Quranic time and prayer term عِشَاء.
The adverbial occurrences are the same lexical item عَشِيّ and are covered under its temporal noun entry.

senses.definition: To turn away from or disregard something.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction عَشَا عَنْ, with the object expressed as the remembrance or admonition of God.

senses.definition: To be blind to something, or to act as though one does not see it.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic interpretive use of عَشَا عَنْ; the expression presents disregard in the imagery of impaired or feigned sight.

senses.definition: The latter part of the day: afternoon or evening, extending in some contexts toward nightfall.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a temporal noun and adverb; Quranic contexts may render it as afternoon, evening, or, in an evening–night pairing, at night.

senses.definition: An evening, or the late part of a particular day.
senses.usage_conditions: The form عَشِيَّة commonly specifies the evening belonging to one particular day.

senses.definition: Nightfall; the beginning or early darkness of night.
senses.usage_conditions: The term can denote the period from sunset toward the onset of deeper night and is used for the early-night time.
A conventional religious use, especially in the expression صَلَاةُ العِشَاءِ or elliptically العِشَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat the evening meal; of camels, to eat the evening pasture or evening feed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed someone the evening meal or feed, or to pasture camels by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use involving a person or animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To repair or betake oneself by night toward a person, object, or fire, seeking its light or guidance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The fire-related construction may include approaching from afar in weak light and hoping to obtain guidance or good.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn away from the fire or its light and go elsewhere.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction with عَنْ expressing departure from the source of light.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become weak-sighted, especially in darkness, or to become blind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical evidence includes reduced sight by night, poor sight by day and night, and complete loss of sight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wrong, injure, treat unjustly, or tyrannically.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or extended Form I construction with عَلَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pasture camels with evening feed so that they reach the water already fed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II causative or arranged-pasturing use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act gently, cautiously, or deliberately in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form II construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kindle a fire for birds so that they become dim-sighted and can be captured.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized causative hunting practice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare, marked, and apparently figurative attribution in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone weak-sighted or otherwise affected by impaired sight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed oneself with the evening meal; of animals, to feed or pasture themselves in the evening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive or middle Form V use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone a firebrand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive Form V use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pretend to be weak-sighted or unable to see.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VI use; the lexical evidence also records it in Quran-related exegetical discussion without assigning it a separate QAC form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pretend ignorance of something or deliberately disregard it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form VI construction, like pretending not to see.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To travel at the time of nightfall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII temporal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find someone deviating from the right course or acting wrongfully toward others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X evaluative construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To guide oneself by means of a fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X fire-and-guidance construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bowl of milk drunk when the sheep or goats return from pasture in the evening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weakness, poor quality, or loss of sight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun used substantivally for impaired sight, including darkness affecting the eye and blindness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal, especially a camel, that exceeds others in eating the evening pasture or feed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A possessive-style epithet applied to a male camel; a related feminine form is used for a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Darkness, especially the first darkness of night or the early part of the night; also, nightfall in an adverbial expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The extent of the period is variously described, from the onset of darkness to part of the first quarter of the night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A confused or dubious affair into which one ventures, or a state of perplexity or trial.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for embarking on an unclear matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fire seen from afar at night and approached for its light, or a firebrand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the visible fire or the portable flame itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of perplexity and having little guidance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for confused circumstances or an unclear course of affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of or relating to the time called عَشِيَّة or عَشِيّ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A temporal relational adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of date or palm tree that is late in bearing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man eating the evening meal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal descriptive noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The evening meal or supper; of camels, the evening pasture or evening feed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the fatḥa-initial meal term, distinct from the Quranic عِشَاء for nightfall and its prayer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clouds arriving late in the evening or at eventide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use of the temporal adjective or noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epithet for a camel that continues eating the evening pasture for a long time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels, sheep, or goats that pasture by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural or substantivized use denotes animals characterized by night grazing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or animal that looks and moves by night toward the fire of a person who entertains guests.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fire-seeking descriptive use related to night travel and hospitality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weak-sighted; sightless by night while seeing by day, or having poor sight by night and day.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective for impaired sight, with feminine عَشْوَاء.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epithet for a creature that advances or strikes without seeing where it goes; especially a she-camel that does not see what is before her and strikes things with her forefeet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same epithet is also applied to an eagle that strikes without regard to where it lands.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pursue or undertake an affair at random, without insight, certainty, or concern for the result.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiomatic extension of the heedless movement of the عَشْوَاء.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where one eats the evening meal or supper.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun.

cautions: The Quranic verb form is the supplied يَعْشُ. Its Quranic usage has closely related interpretations of turning away and being blind to or pretending not to see; these are retained as separate senses because the distinction affects interpretation.

The temporal ranges of عَشِيّ and عِشَاء vary somewhat in Classical descriptions. The Quranic entries state the supported late-day, evening, and nightfall uses without treating every broader temporal proposal as a separate Quranic sense.
The vocalized meal term عَشَاء is kept distinct under broader Classical meanings from the Quranic عِشَاء for nightfall and the nightfall prayer.
Historical Lane Quran citation notation was not converted into modern verse locations; Quran examples use only independently supplied QAC locations.
